conventions: Sing forth for the Piel זַמְּרוּ keeps forth with the verb as one phrasal rendering under rule 44, on the reading that forth is part of how the ASV writes the praise-singing rather than a direction the Hebrew does not write; the competing reading marks forth added. This chapter marks no phrasal particle added: 66.12 broughtest out and 66.20 turned away complete their Hiphil lexemes and are settled.
report: Checked all 22 candidate lemmas end to end. Every split in the table is licensed by what the ASV wrote: the suffix renderings (my/I/me/his/him) follow the English pronoun written; the בְּ and לְ unrepresented units are all bare-object recastings (66.4 worship thee, 66.7 observe the nations, 66.13 pay thee) or a reflexive dative (66.7 exalt themselves) under rule 40, while the rendered ones carry a written preposition; the assimilated articles are aligned wherever the ASV writes the (66.7, 66.11) and unrepresented wherever it writes none or an a (66.9, 66.12, 66.14); פֶּה/תְּהִלָּה/תְּפִלָּה differ only by construct position (rectum takes of) or an adverbial accusative taking its supplied with (66.17).

Read the added units, which the table cannot see. 66.16 marks the and of Come and hear added because לְכוּ־שִׁמְעוּ is asyndetic, while 66.5 aligns the and of Come and see to the written waw of וּרְאוּ — a licensed difference, not a split. 66.5 gives the resuming He of He is terrible to אֱלֹהִים written earlier in the verse (rule 25), while 66.7 marks the He of He ruleth added because no nominal stands earlier in that verse; 66.19's He goes to the finite verb under rule 17. All three are the contract's own divisions.

Phrasal particles are consistent: 66.12 broughtest out and 66.20 turned away complete their Hiphil lexemes; 66.2 Sing forth is the one tie (sing alone writes זָמַר) and the verse pass kept forth with the verb and named the competing reading; left as accepted.

66.19 But verily is read as the ASV's one rendering of adversative אָכֵן (gloss nevertheless) rather than a supplied coordinator; no conjunction morpheme stands in the clause and the adversative sense is the lemma's own, so it is not rule 14's added connective. 66.17 aligns he was extolled against the noun רוֹמַם as printed under rule 53's unmarked-divergence sentence; margin read and set aside.
BSB disagreements (66.4 לְ, 66.7 לָמוֹ and בַּ, 66.13 לְ, 66.18 the אֲדֹנָי suffix) are all documented convention differences under rules 40 and 57; none is an error.
No patches, no promotions, no amendments.
